To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

both the molecular and Michel potential, without any adjustment of parameters needed to fit elastic-scattering data at 26.8 MeV, are in most cases able to reproduce simultaneously the absolute cross-section, particularly at large angles where the previous calculations fail to reproduce by orders magnitude, and the angular distribution of cross-section of the 27 Al(α,d)29 Si reaction leading to transitions up to excitation energy of 4.08MeV of the final 29 Si nucleus.

the α-nucleon potential, determined by fitting the elastic-scattering angular distribution data at 26.8 MeV, can be used to calculate the angular distribution of the 29Si(d, α)27Al cross-section at 26.9 MeV with a reasonable degree of agreement with the experimental data.

the α-nuclei interactions are well described by a finite-range macroscopic model and the spectroscopic factors deduced in the 27 Al(α, d ) 29 Si reaction are in good agreement with those deduced from other reactions and with the shell model predictions.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the investigation of α-nuclei interaction using the elastic scattering and inelastic scattering reaction.
the study of α-nucleon interactions in the 27 Al (α,α′) 27 Al elastic scattering and in the 27 A1 (α, d) 29 S1 reaction at 26. 5 and 27.2 MeV incident energy.
a detailed analysis of the 27A1(α,α) and 27A1 (α, d) reactions in the distorted-wave born approximation.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the molecular potential gives a better account of the data than the Michel potential.

the α-nuclei potentials of the Michel and molecular forms are equally effective in the analysis of the reaction data, but the latter has the advantage of being more realistic and physically more meaningful.
the α-nuclei interactions are well described by the two potentials, and that the present analysis is a successful test for the two potentials, particularly for the Michel potential.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the α-27Al molecular and Michel potentials provide a reasonable description of the elastic scattering of α particles and the 27Al(alpha, d)29 Si reaction, and that the α-29Si molecular and Michel potentials are able to describe the α-29 Si elastic scattering and the 27 Al(alpha, d) 29 Si reaction.

the present results, obtained using two α-nucleus optical potentials, support the idea that the α-nuclei potential is a complex potential, with both real and imaginary parts, and with a strong energy dependence.

the present analysis is the first one that can reproduce the reaction cross-sections, simultaneously, for the elastic scattering and the reaction, and that the Michel potential is a better choice than the molecular potential.
The main takeaway from our work is that
, for the first time in the literature, a simultaneous reproduction of the elastic-scattering and inelastic-scattering data is achieved using the same α-nucleus potential.
the molecular α-nucleus potential, in general, gives the best agreement with the experimental cross-sections and angular distributions.

the two α-nucleus interactions, which are used to analyze the elastic scattering data, are able to reproduce simultaneously the absolute cross-section and the angular distribution of the reaction data, and the spectroscopic factor of the ground-state transition.
